title: Intracameral Injection of a Photocrosslinkable Methacrylated Hyaluronic Acid Hydrogel to Establish a Mouse Model of Chronic Ocular Hypertension
authors: Jingchao Li; Shuiqian Wen; Feixiang He; Yuting Gao; Ting Liu
abstract: Background/Objectives: Chronic ocular hypertension (COH) models are essential for glaucoma research. In this study, we established a mouse COH model by in situ photocrosslinking of methacrylated hyaluronic acid (MAHA). Methods: A 2% (w/v) MAHA precursor containing the photoinitiator LAP was injected into the anterior chamber of C57BL/6J mice and crosslinked under 405 nm light to obstruct aqueous outflow. Hydrogel properties, cytocompatibility, intraocular pressure (IOP), Brn3a retinal flat mounts, flash visual evoked potentials (FVEPs), and serum cytokines were assessed; sham-operated and irradiation-only pilot controls were included. Results: The precursor gelled within 30 s (storage modulus ~4100 Pa), lost 97% cell viability. IOP rose from 11.5 ± 0.20 mmHg at baseline to a peak of 24.40 ± 0.67 mmHg (day 12) and remained elevated for 28 days (success rate 60%; failures were surgical complications). Retinal ganglion cell (RGC) loss was ~17% at day 14 and 24–31% at day 28; FVEP P2 amplitude decreased by ~50% with ~30% longer latency; and serum cytokines were unchanged. Pilot controls showed no IOP elevation or RGC loss. Conclusions: A single intracameral MAHA injection induces sustained ocular hypertension with progressive RGC loss and visual pathway dysfunction, without acute ischemic injury, providing a practical model for glaucoma research and neuroprotective drug screening.

title: Coupling Axial Chirality with Through‐Space Charge‐Transfer‐Involved Excited‐State Regulation in Bicarbazole‐Based Blue CP‐OLED Emitters
authors: Si‐Wei Chen; Zijian Chen; Weihao Liu; Mengke Li; Qianyu He; Yingrui Tian; Yu Fu; Xuewei Nie; Juntao Hu; Lu Zhou; Shaofu Chen; Qingyue Guo; Junji Kido; Shi‐Jian Su
abstract: ABSTRACT Blue circularly polarized organic light‐emitting diodes (CP‐OLEDs) remain challenging because efficient triplet harvesting and strong electroluminescence dissymmetry must be achieved within a single chiral emitter. Herein, an axial‐chirality‐assisted thermally activated delayed fluorescence emitter, Zooey‐TRZ, is developed by incorporating a sterically constrained bicarbazole‐based chiral axis with the triazine acceptor. The axially locked bicarbazole scaffold participates directly in the electronic structure, giving rise to through‐space charge‐transfer‐involved excited states, a reduced singlet‐triplet energy gap, and spin‐orbit coupling‐active triplet‐to‐singlet conversion pathways. In doped films, concentration‐ and host‐polarity‐dependent interactions regulate excited‐state energetics and reverse intersystem crossing, while stronger environmental polarity weakens circularly polarized luminescence, revealing a balance between triplet harvesting and chiroptical response. Single‐crystal analysis suggests slipped donor‐acceptor packing consistent with J‐aggregation‐like interactions. Enantiopure CP‐OLEDs exhibit blue electroluminescence at 455 nm, maximum external quantum efficiencies of 21.14% and 20.42%, and opposite electroluminescence dissymmetry factors of +7.03 × 10 −3 and −7.05 × 10 −3 . These results establish axially locked bicarbazole as an effective platform for excited‐state engineering in efficient blue circularly polarized emitters.

title: Stretchable helical fiber sensor with human motion monitoring capability for mandibular motion assessment in temporomandibular disorders
authors: Bingran Du; Yue Zhai; Ankang Du; Fang Li; Mengfei Zhu; Mingbo Tian; Lijun Lu
abstract: Temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) are prevalent musculoskeletal conditions affecting the orofacial region. Wearable monitoring of mandibular motion may facilitate clinical assessment of TMDs. To satisfy this critical demand, this work proposes a highly stretchable and sensitive sensing strategy via the integration of a graphite nanosheet conductive ink with flexible fibers featuring a unique helical architecture, enabling the construction of a stretchable helical fiber sensor (HFS). The effective integration between the conductive layer and the fiber substrate was confirmed by microscopic morphological characterization. Performance evaluations demonstrated that the HFS possesses a low strain-detection limit of 0.5%, a rapid response time of 33 ms, and excellent stability over 10,000 deformation cycles. In practical demonstrations, the HFS recorded different motion-related signals from blinking to jumping and mandibular-motion-related strain signals in three illustrative cases (one with bilaterally normal temporomandibular joints and two with unilateral disc displacement with reduction). These findings support the preliminary feasibility of the HFS as a wearable tool for the adjunctive assessment of TMD-related mandibular motion, although validation in larger cohorts using established reference methods is required.

title: Piezoelectric and optical fluorescent stretchable electrospun nanocomposite: part of secured-solar room
authors: Remya Nair; Dania Hosny; Fatemah Abuelhassan; Basil Alothman; Mohamed Trabelsi; Marwa Saad; Sneha Bhagyaraj; Germein Magdy; Patrik Sobolciak; Anton Popelka; Zainab Abelhassan; Nader Shehata
venue: Sensors and Communication Technologies in the 1 GHz to 10 THz Band III
abstract: Cerium Oxide (ceria) nanoparticle is considered one of the most promising optoelectronic materials due to optical visible fluorescence emission and its wide applications in optical sensors and biomarkers as free radical scavengers. Ceria has been added in different nanofibers to form optoelectronic multi-functional nanocomposite. Among different organic nanofibers, polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) has a remarkable electroactive β-sheets as a promising piezoelectric mat that can be used in sustainable energy-harvesting devices and vibration sensors. The optical fluorescence of a ceria nanoparticle nanocomposite inserted during-situ within electrospun PVDF nanofibers is examined in this study. A blue shift in the ceria NPs' bandgap was discovered by optical absorbance analysis, which also improved UV absorption in the PVDF polymer in the vicinity of 3 eV. Luminosity investigation showed a progressive fluorescence effect at some additive doses, with a visible emission of 520 nm under optical stimulation of 430 nm. In addition, ceria nanoparticles improve the piezoelectric response of the nanocomposite as a nucleating agent for better dipole alignment of PVDF with β-sheets concentration of around 60%. Mechanical properties of the formed nanocomposite allow a breaking elongation more than 50%, which is much more stretchability enhanced compared to pure PVDF nanofibers mat. The synthesized nanocomposite therefore provides a multifunctional platform for piezoelectric energy harvesting and optical sensing in cyber-secured smart environments. To extend the material-level characterization toward practical application, a Solar Room framework is demonstrated in which a 5 × 5 PZT footstep matrix provides supplementary harvested energy through power conditioning and storage for low-power IoT monitoring, while secure telemetry mechanisms support cyber-secured operation. This multilevel framework connects flexible nanocomposite functionality with the practical requirements of harvested-energy utilization and secure IoT integration.
